parole.significato: A requiem mass or other commemoration of a deceased person held one month after burial.
parole.testo: From Middle English monethes mynde under influence from Medieval Latin dies mensis (“day of the month”) and Old English ġemynd, whose principal sense was "memory".

From Medieval Latin portgravius, from Old English portgerēfa &c., from port + gerēfa (“reeve”).

parole.significato: A soc (a medieval right to hold a court or to receive fines).
parole.testo: From Middle English soke, from Medieval Latin (Anglo-Latin) sōca "right of jurisdiction", from Old English sōcn (“jurisdiction, prosecution”, literally “act of seeking”), from Proto-West Germanic *sōkni, from Proto-Germanic *sōkniz (“seeking, inquiry”), from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂g- (“to track”).

parole.significato: An Anglo-Saxon copper coin of little value, used in Northumbria.
parole.testo: From Medieval Latin styca, from Old English stycas, styċġċe pl, Northumbrian variants of Old English styċċe (“small piece of money; bit; piece”).
Perhaps via Medieval Latin *trappa, from Old English træppe /treppe (“trap, snare”), from Proto-Germanic *trap-, from Proto-Indo-European *dreb-, from *der- (“to walk, step”).
